paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose it is proposed that all university students should be required to learn academic writing. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 方向：假设建议所有大学生都必须学习学术写作。您现在需要写一份回复，说明您对该提案的看法。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明： 在本节中，您将听到三则新闻报道。在每篇新闻报道的最后，你都会听到两到三个问题。新闻报道和提问均只发言一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some music inspires you to move your feet, some inspires you to get out there and change the world. In any case, it’s 26 to say that music moves people in special ways.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有些音乐激励你迈出脚步，有些音乐激励你走出去改变世界。无论如何，可以公平地说，音乐以特殊的方式打动人们。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you’re especially into a piece of music, your brain does something called Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response (ASMR), which 27 to you like a sting in your brain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果您特别喜欢一首音乐，您的大脑会执行一种称为自主感觉经络反应 (ASMR) 的操作，这对您来说就像大脑中的刺痛一样。

paragraphs.sourceText: It turns out that ASMR is pretty special. According to a 28 published study in The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer’s Disease, the part of your brain responsible for ASMR doesn’t get lost to Alzheimer’s. Alzheimer’s 29 to put people into layers of confusion, and the study confirms that music can sometimes 30 lift people out of the Alzheimer’s haze and bring them back to (at least a likeness of) normality ... if only for a short while. ASMR is powerful stuff!
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实证明，ASMR 相当特别。根据《阿尔茨海默病预防杂志》最近发表的一项研究，大脑中负责 ASMR 的部分不会因阿尔茨海默病而消失。阿尔茨海默氏症往往会让人们陷入层层困惑，研究证实，音乐有时确实可以让人们摆脱阿尔茨海默氏症的阴霾，让他们恢复（至少是相似的）正常状态……哪怕只是短暂的一段时间。 ASMR 很强大！

paragraphs.sourceText: This phenomenon has been 31 several times but rarely studied properly. One of the most famous examples of this is the story of 92-year-old Henry Dryer, who comes out of dementia (痴呆) while listening to songs from his youth.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种现象已被多次观察到，但很少得到适当的研究。最著名的例子之一是 92 岁的亨利·德里尔 (Henry Dryer) 的故事，他在听着年轻时的歌曲时摆脱了痴呆症。

paragraphs.sourceText: Jeff Anderson, associate professor in Radiology at the University of Utah and 32 author on the study, says “In our society, the diagnoses of dementia are 33 resources to the maximum. No one says playing music will be a cure for Alzheimer’s disease, but it might make the symptoms more 34 ，decrease the cost of care and improve a patient’s 35 of life.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 犹他大学放射学副教授、该研究的撰稿人杰夫·安德森（Jeff Anderson）表示：“在我们的社会中，痴呆症的诊断正在最大限度地消耗资源。没有人说演奏音乐可以治愈阿尔茨海默病，但它可能会使症状更容易控制，降低护理成本并提高患者的生活质量。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Can playing video games help you get a better job?
paragraphs.translationZh: 玩电子游戏可以帮助你找到更好的工作吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) The gaming industry is larger than films and music combined, yet few of us are likely to list our achievements in playing computer games as work experience in our résumé. But why not? Businesses are waking up to the skills gamers can bring to the workplace.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 游戏行业比电影和音乐加起来还要大，但很少有人会在简历中将玩电脑游戏的成就列为工作经验。但为什么不呢？企业正在意识到游戏玩家可以为工作场所带来的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) One start-up is convinced that the skills learned by playing games — hard-won through years of training and battle — can be applied to real-life work situations. And Game Academy reckons its belief is backed up by hard data. Do you enjoy unusual puzzle games like Portal, or tower defence games like Defense Grid? The team has found that IT workers play those more than average. But if you prefer Civilization, Total War, or X-Com, where strategy and resource management are key, then you might have more in common with managers.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 一家初创企业坚信，通过玩游戏学到的技能（通过多年的训练和战斗来之不易）可以应用于现实生活中的工作情况。游戏学院认为其信念是有确凿数据支持的。您喜欢像 Portal 这样不寻常的益智​​游戏，还是像 Def​​ense Grid 这样的塔防游戏？该团队发现，IT 员工玩这些游戏的频率高于平均水平。但如果你更喜欢《文明》、《全面战争》或《幽浮》，其中战略和资源管理是关键，那么你可能与管理者有更多共同点。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Game Academy’s idea is simple: analyse gamers’ habits from their online gaming profile, and offer courses in valuable skills that reflect their aptitudes — skills they can practise and refine in-game. And there is already a growing acceptance that gaming skills are transferable.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 游戏学院的想法很简单：从玩家的在线游戏资料中分析他们的习惯，并提供反映他们才能的宝贵技能课程——他们可以在游戏中练习和完善的技能。人们已经越来越多地接受游戏技能是可以转移的。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Even the military is hiring gamers. “The ability to absorb information, react swiftly and coordinate actions whilst remaining calm under pressure are often attributes of people that are good at gaming,” according to a Royal Air Force spokesperson. Those skills are part of what the Royal Air Force is looking for “in a variety of roles”. “Skills acquired through gaming can be very relevant to certain areas.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D）甚至军队也在招聘游戏玩家。英国皇家空军发言人表示：“善于博弈的人通常具有吸收信息、迅速反应和协调行动的能力，同时在压力下保持冷静。”这些技能是英国皇家空军正在寻找的“各种角色”的一部分。 “通过游戏获得的技能可能与某些领域非常相关。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) “There are plenty of soft skills that gamers can utilise in a professional setting, such as teamwork, problem solving and strategic planning,” says Ryan Gardner, a regional director with Hays recruitment. But does that really mean your top 100 ranking in Overwatch should go down in your résumé? “It’s about how you either make it relevant to the job you are applying for, or how it makes you more interesting as a potential employee,” Mr Gardner says.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) “游戏玩家可以在专业环境中运用很多软技能，例如团队合作、解决问题和战略规划，”Hays 招聘区域总监 Ryan Gardner 说道。但这真的意味着你的《守望先锋》前 100 名排名应该在你的简历中下降吗？加德纳先生说：“关键在于你如何让它与你正在申请的工作相关，或者它如何让你作为一名潜在员工变得更有趣。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Two years ago, a Glasgow University study made headlines for suggesting gaming could make students more successful. But “the research hasn’t really changed minds, at least not yet,” says one of the authors of the study, Dr Matthew Barr. He’s now writing a book on the topic. “For now, I think the negative reputation around games means that telling someone you’re a determined gamer is more likely to harm your chances of getting a job. But if someone can explain how they’ve led a team in an online game, for example, they may be able to persuade an employer that this is useful,” says Dr Barr.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 两年前，格拉斯哥大学的一项研究因表明游戏可以让学生更加成功而成为头条新闻。但“这项研究并没有真正改变人们的想法，至少现在还没有，”该研究的作者之一马修·巴尔博士说。他现在正在写一本关于这个主题的书。 “目前，我认为围绕游戏的负面声誉意味着告诉某人你是一名坚定的游戏玩家更有可能损害你找到工作的机会。但如果有人能够解释他们如何在网络游戏中领导团队，他们可能能够说服雇主这很有用，”巴尔博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Playing games casually is unlikely to help your career prospects. But part of Game Academy’s suggestion is to transform casual gamers into “conscious” ones, applying critical thinking to developing their skills. “We see gameplay as a resource of talent,” says co-founder David Barrie. “Why can’t we put in our résumé our gaming victories and achievements?” he asks. “If they say they want leadership — why can’t I point to my years of leading World of Warcraft raids?”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 随便玩游戏不太可能对你的职业前景有帮助。但游戏学院建议的一部分是将休闲玩家转变为“有意识”的玩家，运用批判性思维来发展他们的技能。 “我们将游戏玩法视为一种人才资源，”联合创始人大卫·巴里 (David Barrie) 说道。 “为什么我们不能把我们的游戏胜利和成就写进简历呢？”他问道。 “如果他们说他们想要领导——为什么我不能指出我多年来领导《魔兽世界》突袭的经历呢？”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) There are already plenty of gamers out there who know that their hobby has made them who they are. Earlier this year, Matthew Ricci told gaming site Kotaku: “If you’re playing EVE Online you basically already have an MBA.” Often made fun of in gaming circles as a “spreadsheet simulator (电子表格模拟)”, the economy of the fictional EVE universe is driven by real market principles. If you want to build a new spaceship, the raw material has to be mined by another player. Manufacturing costs come into effect, and commodities fluctuate in price based on demand and the distance to haul the commodity.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 已经有很多游戏玩家知道他们的爱好造就了他们。今年早些时候，马修·里奇 (Matthew Ricci) 告诉游戏网站 Kotaku：“如果你玩《EVE Online》，那么你基本上已经拥有了 MBA 学位。”虚构的 EVE 宇宙的经济是由真实的市场原则驱动的，在游戏圈中经常被戏称为“电子表格模拟”。如果你想建造一艘新的宇宙飞船，原材料就必须由其他玩家开采。制造成本生效，商品价格根据需求和运输商品的距离而波动。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Mr Ricci, who had always dreamed of being the boss of his own company, ran an in-game corporation comprising hundreds of players. Eventually, he realised he could transfer his skills to real-life business — instead of doing it for free. He restructured Zentech, once a taxation vehicle for his father’s business, and it is now in its fourth year helping international brands enter the Canadian market. EVE teaches skills like creativity, leadership, organisation, and conflict resolution, he maintains. He credits his success to his family, his strong desire to run his own business — and “a damn good company in Iceland that made a damn good game”.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 里奇先生一直梦想成为自己公司的老板，经营着一家由数百名玩家组成的游戏公司。最终，他意识到他可以将自己的技能转移到现实生活中的业务中，而不是免费做。他重组了 Zentech，这家公司曾经是他父亲企业的税务工具，现在已经是帮助国际品牌进入加拿大市场的第四个年头了。他坚持认为，《EVE》教授创造力、领导力、组织力和解决冲突等技能。他将自己的成功归功于他的家庭、他经营自己企业的强烈愿望以及“冰岛一家非常好的公司，制作了一款非常棒的游戏”。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Digital entrepreneur and business consultant Mia Bennett says: “In more traditional settings, gaming is still imagined to be the pursuit of teenage boys — a waste of time.” But there are some links to skills like “decision-making, the ability to anticipate and future planning,” she says. “It also helps with meta-skills — learning how to learn, experimentation, and creative thinking.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 数字企业家兼商业顾问 Mia Bennett 表示：“在更传统的环境中，游戏仍然被认为是十几岁男孩的追求——浪费时间。”但她说，这与“决策、预测能力和未来规划”等技能有一些联系。 “它还有助于培养元技能——学习如何学习、实验和创造性思维。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Twelve years into his career, Mark Long, a radiotherapy physicist with the NHS in Surrey, doesn’t get as much gaming time as he used to. “I would love to say that my gaming skills allow me to destroy cancer using linear accelerators like photon (光子) blasters, but that’s not quite the reality.” Instead, he credits old-school games like Palace of Magic with exposing him to computers. Every new gaming upgrade improved his knowledge of how they worked. Gaming also encouraged a competitive spirit — and that, he believes, translates. “When creating treatment plans, the aim is to optimise the radiation dose to the tumour and restrict it as much as possible to healthy surrounding tissues and organs,” he says. It’s about “repeating the process, but each time doing something slightly different to improve the result”. Not unlike achieving a high score or a perfect run. “Most videogames are essentially puzzles to solve,” he says. “And problem-solving is a big part of my job.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 萨里郡 NHS 的放射治疗物理学家马克·朗 (Mark Long) 职业生涯十二年后，并没有像以前那样获得那么多的游戏时间。 “我很想说，我的游戏技能使我能够使用光子爆破器等线性加速器来消灭癌症​​，但这并不完全是现实。”相反，他认为《魔宫》等老派游戏让他接触到了电脑。每一次新的游戏升级都加深了他对游戏运作方式的了解。游戏还鼓励了竞争精神——他相信这一点也能得到体现。 “制定治疗计划时，目标是优化肿瘤的辐射剂量，并尽可能限制其对周围健康组织和器官的辐射剂量，”他说。它是关于“重复这个过程，但每次都做一些稍微不同的事情来改善结果”。与获得高分或完美跑步没什么不同。 “大多数电子游戏本质上都是需要解决的谜题，”他说。 “解决问题是我工作的重要组成部分。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) “Over at Game Academy, Mr Barrie is aware they still have a mountain to climb. The employer community will need the science,” he says, but confesses he only became a true believer when he started asking players about their biggest in-game achievements. “The scale and scope of their answers were amazing,” he says. “But ask them the same about their work, and they don’t know.” “The engagement and powerful skills that people get playing a game — why can’t work be like that?” he asks.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) “在游戏学院，巴里先生意识到他们还有一座山需要攀登。雇主社区需要科学，”他说，但他承认，当他开始向玩家询问他们在游戏中最大的成就时，他才成为真正的信徒。 “他们的答案的规模和范围令人惊叹，”他说。 “但问他们同样的工作，他们却说不知道。” “人们通过玩游戏获得的参与度和强大的技能——为什么工作不能像这样呢？”他问道。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Certain gaming skills meet the requirements of the armed forces in Britain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 某些游戏技能符合英国武装部队的要求。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. One veteran player has applied his gaming skills to his real-world business and owes his success partly to a game company.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 一位资深玩家将自己的游戏技能运用到了现实世界的业务中，他的成功部分归功于一家游戏公司。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. According to a researcher, bad reputation about games will probably limit a gamer’s chances of landing a job.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 据一位研究人员称，游戏的不良声誉可能会限制游戏玩家找到工作的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Businesses are beginning to realise gaming skills are applicable to their employees’ work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 企业开始意识到游戏技能适用于员工的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. A physicist admits gaming has contributed to his computer knowledge and skills of solving problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 一位物理学家承认游戏有助于提高他的计算机知识和解决问题的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Game Academy proposes to help gamers develop their skills using critical thinking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 游戏学院建议帮助玩家利用批判性思维培养技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. One who enjoys playing games that require management skills to win might possess more qualities of a manager.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 喜欢玩需要管理技能才能获胜的游戏的人可能拥有更多的管理者素质。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. In more conventional views, gaming is a time-wasting activity pursued by young boys.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 在更传统的观点中，游戏是小男孩进行的一项浪费时间的活动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. It is suggested that gaming skills be included in a résumé if they enhance a job applicant’s appeal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 如果游戏技能能够增强求职者的吸引力，建议将其纳入简历中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Many gamers know their passion for playing games has shaped their identity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 许多游戏玩家知道他们对玩游戏的热情塑造了他们的身份。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Junk food is now a staple of many Americans’ diets. Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. Bad diets are.
paragraphs.translationZh: 垃圾食品现在已成为许多美国人饮食的主食。休闲食品公司的广告活动通常以体育明星为主角，传达这样的信息：我们只需进行更多的体育锻炼就可以消除食用其产品的任何负面影响。但最近的研究表明，缺乏锻炼并不是肥胖率上升的原因。不良饮食是。

paragraphs.sourceText: Interventions (干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers. Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat. Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach.
paragraphs.translationZh: 帮助减少垃圾食品消费的干预措施对于儿童和青少年尤其重要。预防胜于治疗，因为肥胖很难治疗。不幸的是，虽然健康教育在幼儿中取得了一些成功，但青少年却很难接触到。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers’ attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers’ instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，一项大规模研究尝试了一种创新方法来改变青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果令人鼓舞。研究人员认为，之前的干预措施可能因一个重大缺陷而失败：他们着眼于未来、更健康的你，并认为这对青少年来说就足够了。相比之下，新的干预措施巧妙地利用了青少年的叛逆和自主本能，以及他们对社会正义的重视。

paragraphs.sourceText: To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy. The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm for these vulnerable groups. Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to “fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food”
paragraphs.translationZh: 为此，研究人员让学生阅读一篇有关食品行业的文章。它揭示了一个秘密，即用于使垃圾食品更容易上瘾并将产品描述为健康的操纵和欺骗策略。文章还解释了广告活动如何专门针对非常年轻和贫困的人，从而对这些弱势群体造成伤害。随后，参与者阅读了一份针对青少年的虚构调查，这些青少年希望“通过购买和少吃加工食品来反击这些公司”

paragraphs.sourceText: After the intervention, participants associated healthy eating with autonomy and social justice. The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing. Importantly, there were also some promising effects of the new intervention on actual behavior. A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. The teens chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) more often over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda). Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers’ own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 干预后，参与者将健康饮食与自主性和社会正义联系起来。青少年还认为健康饮食更有吸引力。重要的是，新的干预措施对实际行为也产生了一些有希望的影响。一天后，学生们在看似无关的环境中选择了零食和饮料。青少年更常选择健康的零食和饮料（如水果或水），而不是不健康的选择（如饼干和苏打水）。显然，将健康饮食与青少年自身价值观联系起来似乎是预防肥胖的一个有希望的途径。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.
paragraphs.translationZh: 成人在快速眼动睡眠期间会做梦，而婴儿则有大量的快速眼动睡眠。因此，可以公平地假设婴儿有很多梦想。

paragraphs.sourceText: But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但科学家认为，对于新生儿和婴儿来说，快速眼动睡眠的目的与做梦完全不同。当婴儿处于快速眼动睡眠阶段时，他们的大脑可以发展出通路、联系，并最终学习语言。

paragraphs.sourceText: Since your baby doesn’t dream at this stage of brain development, it’s safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma (创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于您的宝宝在大脑发育的这个阶段不会做梦，因此可以安全地假设宝宝也不会做噩梦。噩梦源于创伤、过度活跃的想象力以及日常生活中的正常压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? Good question, but the answer is nothing! So, when do babies start dreaming? The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你想知道，婴儿会梦见什么吗？好问题，但答案是什么都没有！那么，宝宝什么时候开始做梦呢？人们普遍认为，他们在两岁左右就开始做梦了。心理学家大卫·福克斯（David Foulkes）对儿童（从很小的孩子到青少年）进行研究，以揭示他们梦想的秘密。在他的实验室里，他让孩子们入睡，然后每晚叫醒他们 3 次，并要求他们描述所记得的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: Foulkes’ findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.
paragraphs.translationZh: 福克斯的发现并不令人意外。基本上，小孩子都有小梦想。但孩子们在做梦时看到的具体内容取决于他们的年龄。随着孩子的成长，他们的梦想也在成长。

paragraphs.sourceText: Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots (快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. According to Foulkes, “Children’s dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration.” Kids ages 5 – 9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. Still, that’s not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes’ studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.
paragraphs.translationZh: 很小的孩子的梦通常只是快照，与成年人的梦相比，看起来更像是幻灯片而不是电影。它们以动物和其他熟悉的景象为特色，比如人们吃饭的图像。福克斯说，“孩子们的梦想生活……似乎与他们清醒时的想象和叙述相似。” 5 至 9 岁的孩子开始看到活动的图像和角色。现在的梦想包括多个事件一个接一个地串联在一起。他们也开始发展出更强的记住梦境的能力。不过，情况并非总是如此：在福克斯的研究中，当在快速眼动睡眠期间被唤醒时，25% 的孩子不记得做过梦，这种趋势一直持续到 9 岁。

paragraphs.sourceText: So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，如果您的宝宝在睡觉时似乎处于压力状态或醒来后感到不安，可能还有其他因素在起作用。

paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 对于醒来后表现出不安的婴儿，我们可以采取什么假设？
